children: The equity benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty bounced back sharply on Friday, tracking a rally in Asian markets after four consecutive sessions of losses.
Fading expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike this month lifted global equities and pulled bond yields lower.
At around 10:45 a.m., the Sensex was up 580.08 points or 0.76 percent at 76,732.94, while the broader Nifty advanced to 23,961.75, up 88.30 points or 0.37 percent.
The Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 gained 0.6 percent and 0.2 percent, respectively.
Key factors behind market rise
1) Positive global cues

: The rebound in domestic equities came amid a broad-based rally across Asian markets. Hong Kong's Hang Seng climbed 2 percent, South Korea's KOSPI advanced 1.3 percent, Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 1.11 percent and Shanghai's SSE Composite index traded 0.35 percent higher.

US markets had ended more than 1 percent higher in overnight deals on Thursday, setting a positive tone for Asian equities. Wall Street futures were also trading higher on Friday morning, indicating a firm start for US equities.
2) Fed rate-hike bets ease

: US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has said he would support keeping interest rates unchanged at the US central bank's next policy meeting if upcoming data confirms that inflation pressures are easing.
3) Decline in India VIX

: The fear gauge, or volatility index, declined more than 4 percent to 10.85. A fall in the India VIX indicates lower expected market volatility and suggests easing near-term uncertainty for investors.
4) Rupee rises

: The rupee gained 5 paise to 94.46 against the US dollar, supported by optimism over rising foreign inflows and a rise in risk appetite. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.53 against the US dollar and then gained ground to touch 94.46, registering a gain of 5 paise from its previous close.
5) Buying in capital market stocks
: Capital-market stocks rallied after SEBI signalled changes to the derivatives settlement-price mechanism following volatility triggered by the new closing auction.
BSE jumped 4.5 percent, Angel One gained 5.4 percent and Groww rose 2.5 percent, while Nuvama Wealth and Motilal Oswal added 1.2 percent each.
SEBI said it would issue a consultation paper on revising the mechanism.
6) Value buying
: Value buying emerged at lower levels after four consecutive sessions of losses as investors stepped in to buy shares at lower levels.
The Nifty and Sensex had fallen 1.3 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively, over the previous four sessions as rising crude prices and bond yields hurt sentiment.
